keykeeperExpiringItemsReportDesc.message: Items that have expired or expire in the next 30 days: API keys, certificates, licenses, cards, and anything you set an expiration date on.

keykeeperNoExpiringItems.message: No items have expired or expire in the next 30 days.

keykeeperExpiringItemsFoundDesc.message: These items have expired or expire in the next 30 days. Renew or rotate them, then update their expiration dates.

keykeeperVersionsUnreadable.message: Earlier versions that can't be opened: $COUNT$

keykeeperRestoreVersionDesc.message: The item goes back to how it was on $DATE$. How it is now stays in its version history, so you can come back to it.

keykeeperVersionSameAsNow.message: This version looks the same as the item does now.

keykeeperVersionHistoryWhoSees.message: Everyone who can open this item can see its earlier versions, including old passwords.

keykeeperVersionHistoryHiddenPasswords.message: You can't see this item's passwords, so its earlier versions show only when they were saved and by whom.

keykeeperClearHistoryDesc.message: Its earlier versions are deleted for everyone who can open it. The item stays as it is now.

keykeeperDeleteVersionDesc.message: The version from $DATE$ is deleted for everyone who can open this item.

keykeeperClearedHistoryItemId.message: Cleared the earlier versions of item $ID$.

keykeeperEventStreamAdded.message: Started sending the organization's events to a new place.

keykeeperEventStreamChanged.message: Changed a place the organization's events are sent.

keykeeperEventStreamRemoved.message: Stopped sending the organization's events to a place.

keykeeperEventStreamStopped.message: The server turned off a place the organization's events are sent: sending there kept failing.

keykeeperDeletedVersionItemId.message: Deleted an earlier version of item $ID$.

keykeeperManageAccountRecoveryHint.message: Can reset the master password of members in account recovery, and so sign in as them and see everything they can.

keykeeperImportExportHint.message: Covers import. Exporting the organization's items needs access to all items, which custom roles can't have yet.

keykeeperCustomRoleNoCollections.message: With these permissions, a custom role can't also manage all shared folders yet. Give them shared folders on the Shared folders tab.

keykeeperBiometricsNotEnrolled.message: Unlock with biometrics is still off. It wasn't confirmed, or the desktop app isn't running.

keykeeperSelfHostedAddressHint.message: Your server's address, such as vault.example.com.

keykeeperAccessIntro.message: Who can open each shared folder, and how. Owners and admins see every item. Everyone else opens the shared folders they're given, directly or through a group. Someone who reaches a folder two ways gets, for each permission, the more open way, so passwords stay hidden only if every way hides them.

keykeeperAccessHiddenFolder.message: 1 shared folder isn't shown, since you can't open it yourself.

keykeeperAccessHiddenFolders.message: $COUNT$ shared folders aren't shown, since you can't open them yourself.

keykeeperAccessSearch.message: Search people, groups, and shared folders

keykeeperAccessEveryItemPeople.message: Also open to everyone who sees every item: $NAMES$.

keykeeperAccessOnlyEveryItemPeople.message: Only people who see every item can open it: $NAMES$.

keykeeperAccessNoFoldersYet.message: This organization has no shared folders yet.

keykeeperAccessLoadFailed.message: Couldn't load who can see what. Reload the page to try again.

keykeeperCanViewHidden.message: Can view but not see passwords

keykeeperCanEditHidden.message: Can edit but not see passwords

keykeeperCapSeePasswordsHint.message: Passwords, codes, card numbers, and ID numbers. Without it, people can still fill these into web pages, and a page can read what's filled.

keykeeperGridAppsEnforce.message: The server enforces the rest; see passwords, export, share, and print are up to the apps, since anyone who can open an item could copy it with other tools.

keykeeperGridManageIncludesAll.message: Managing a shared folder includes every other permission in it.

keykeeperGridNeedsSeePasswords.message: Export, print, and share need see passwords.

keykeeperReachFoldersRevoked.message: Before they were revoked, $NAME$ could open $FOLDERS$ with $ITEMS$.

keykeeperReachEveryItem.message: $NAME$ can see every item in this organization: $ITEMS$.

keykeeperReachEveryItemRevoked.message: Before they were revoked, $NAME$ could see every item in this organization: $ITEMS$.

keykeeperReachNoFoldersRevoked.message: Before they were revoked, $NAME$ couldn't open any shared folders.

keykeeperReachNeverConfirmed.message: $NAME$ was never confirmed, so they never had the key to this organization's items.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsIntro.message: $NAME$ could see these logins' passwords in the shared folders they could open. They may still know them, so change them.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsEveryItem.message: $NAME$ could see every item in this organization, so they may know any of its passwords.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsOtherItems.message: Other items they could see, such as notes and cards, aren't listed.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsNotAgain.message: This list won't be shown again, so copy it if you'll need it later.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsAccessLink.message: See who can open each shared folder

keykeeperExposedPrivacy.message: Each password is checked against Have I Been Pwned's list of breached passwords without sending it: only the first 5 characters of its SHA-1 hash leave your browser, the answer lists hundreds of possible matches, and the match is made here.

keykeeperExposedUnchecked.message: $COUNT$ items couldn't be checked for breaches, because this browser couldn't reach api.pwnedpasswords.com. It may be offline, or a firewall may block it. Try again later.

keykeeperHealthToFix.message: $COUNT$ items to fix: weak, reused, or exposed passwords

keykeeperExposedCheckFailed.message: Couldn't check this password, because this browser couldn't reach api.pwnedpasswords.com. It may be offline, or a firewall may block it.

keykeeperBreachCheckAfterUnlock.message: Check my passwords against known breaches after unlocking

keykeeperBreachCheckAfterUnlockHint.message: For the count beside Health (for MSP staff, every client item you can edit) and the MSP console's Exposed column. Each check sends Have I Been Pwned the first 5 characters of each password's SHA-1 hash. Turned off, nothing is sent unless you open the exposed passwords report or press Check. Creating or changing your master password checks it the same way while "Check known data breaches for this password" is ticked there, as it is at first.

keykeeperHealthToFixOne.message: 1 item to fix: a weak, reused, or exposed password

keykeeperExposedUncheckedOne.message: 1 item couldn't be checked for breaches, because this browser couldn't reach api.pwnedpasswords.com. It may be offline, or a firewall may block it. Try again later.

keykeeperServerAddressHint.message: Just the address. We add https:// for you.

keykeeperServerAddressInvalid.message: That isn't a server address. Try one like vault.example.com.

keykeeperNewHereInvite.message: New here? Your admin sends the invite.

keykeeperServerAddressOnly.message: Use just the server's address, without @, ? or #.

keykeeperCustomServerAddresses.message: This browser uses custom server addresses.

keykeeperRestoreVersionDropsPasskey.message: The item goes back to how it was on $DATE$. How it is now stays in its version history, so you can come back to it. This version doesn't have its passkey for $PASSKEY$: restoring removes it, and you can't sign in with it after.

keykeeperRestoreVersionDropsPasskeys.message: The item goes back to how it was on $DATE$. How it is now stays in its version history, so you can come back to it. This version doesn't have $COUNT$ of its passkeys (for $PASSKEYS$): restoring removes them, and you can't sign in with them after.

keykeeperRestoreFailed.message: Couldn't restore it. If the item changed since you opened it, go back and try again.

keykeeperCantMoveItem.message: Your organization doesn't let you move it to another shared folder.

keykeeperCantCopyItem.message: Your organization doesn't let you copy this item.

keykeeperSsoLinkInWebVault.message: Your organization requires single sign-on, and your account isn't linked to it yet. Sign in to the web vault with your email and master password to link it, then sign in here with single sign-on.

keykeeperLinkSsoVerify.message: Confirm it's you to link your account to this organization's single sign-on. Microsoft then asks which account to use, and you confirm it before anything is linked.

keykeeperTwoStepSetupInWebVault.message: Two-step login is required for your role by $NAMES$. Sign in to the web vault at $URL$ to set it up with an authenticator app, a security key or passkey, or Duo, then sign in here again.

keykeeperTwoStepSetupInWebVaultUnnamed.message: Two-step login is required for your role. Sign in to the web vault at $URL$ to set it up with an authenticator app, a security key or passkey, or Duo, then sign in here again.

keykeeperAdminTwoStepOn.message: Turned on two-step login for admins.

keykeeperAdminTwoStepOff.message: Turned off two-step login for admins.

keykeeperAdminTwoStepPolicyDesc.message: Owners, admins, and custom roles that manage members, policies, or account recovery must use an authenticator app, a security key or passkey, or Duo. Email codes don't count. Admins who sign in with the organization's own single sign-on are covered by it there.
